svg.text: Local-First Architecture: Data Model & Sync Layer

g.text: Core Principles
Local is Primary
App works fully offline — server is backup, not source of truth
No Central Authority
Peers sync directly. Conflicts resolved by algorithm, not server.
Merge, Don't Overwrite
All writes eventually converge — CRDT ensures consistency
Instant Reads/Writes
Zero latency — no network round-trip for UI updates
vs Offline-First
Offline-first: server is still source of truth, sync catches up
Local-first: no single source of truth — all copies are equal
Local-first = stronger guarantee (works without server forever)
CRDT Data Layer
CRDT Types for Common Use Cases
G-Counter: distributed increment only (page views)
PN-Counter: increment + decrement (likes, votes)
LWW-Register: last-write-wins per field (settings, status)
OR-Set: add/remove set where add wins (tags, members)
RGA / Yjs Sequence: collaborative text editing
Automerge: JSON-like document CRDT (maps, lists, text)
CRDT property: commutativity + associativity + idempotence → always converges
Sync Protocol (Gossip / Hub)
Hub model: clients sync with server relay (common in practice)
P2P model: clients sync directly via WebRTC (offline mesh)
State sync: exchange full document state (simple, high bandwidth)
Operation sync: exchange deltas / ops (efficient, ordered)
Merkle tree: find diff between two states efficiently
Libraries: Yjs + y-websocket, Automerge, ElectricSQL, PowerSync
Storage Stack
Browser: IndexedDB (persistent, queryable, up to 60% disk)
SQLite via WASM: full SQL local (wa-sqlite, PGlite)
OPFS (Origin Private File System): fast, dedicated file storage
Request persistent storage: navigator.storage.persist() to avoid eviction

svg.text: Trade-off: Complex conflict resolution, storage quotas,
permission model harder (no central auth for reads).
